cold_start.text: Take one breath. Who are you about to stand before?
Leave what is in your hands. Stand fully present.
This moment is between you and Allah.
Set everything down. This is your time.
The world can wait. This cannot.
You are about to stand before the Most High. Arrive fully.

attributes.name: Al-Wakeel
attributes.translation: The Trustee, The Disposer of Affairs

established.text: You are standing before Al-Wakeel — the One who manages every affair better than you ever could. Hand it over.
Your work concerns are real, but you are now in the presence of Al-Muqeet, the One who sustains all things. He has it.
Say 'Nothing will ever befall us except what Allah has destined for us. He is our Protector.' So in Allah let the believers put their trust. - Surah At-Tawbah 9:51
'Tie your camel, then put your trust in Allah.' - Jami' At-Tirmidhi 2517. You're doing the work already, now is the time to focus on trusting Allah.
Whatever concerns you at work: Al-Wakeel already holds it.
You've sometimes noticed thoughts of work drifting into this Salah.
Work has occasionally pulled at your attention during this prayer.

llm_guidance.theme: entrusting affairs and releasing the need to control outcomes
llm_guidance.avoid: productivity advice, toxic positivity, minimising the stress
llm_guidance.tone: grounding, surrendering, confident trust in Allah's management

attributes.name: Ar-Razzaq
attributes.translation: The Provider, The Sustainer of all provision

attributes.name: Al-Mughni
attributes.translation: The Enricher, The One who satisfies all needs

established.text: You are standing before Ar-Razzaq — the One who has already written your provision. Your rizq is guaranteed; your presence here is what matters.
You are standing before Al-Mughni, the One who enriches and satisfies. Every need you carry is known to Him.
Your provision is already written. Come before the One who wrote it.
And He will provide for them from sources they could never imagine. And whoever relies upon Allah — then He alone is sufficient for him. Indeed Allah achieves His Will. - At-Talaq 65:3
If you were to rely upon Allah with the reliance He is due, then He would provide for you just as a bird is provided for — it goes out in the morning empty and returns full. - Jami' At-Tirmidhi 2344
Thoughts of provision have sometimes come during this Salah.
You've occasionally noticed financial worries entering this prayer.

llm_guidance.theme: Allah as the direct and only source of provision — rizq is already written
llm_guidance.avoid: financial advice, vague reassurance, telling them not to worry
llm_guidance.tone: anchoring, certainty in tawakkul, direct connection between the distraction and the attribute

attributes.name: Al-Hafeez
attributes.translation: The Protector, The Preserver of all things

attributes.name: Al-Amaan
attributes.translation: The Giver of Security and Refuge

established.text: You are standing before Al-Hafeez — the One who is already guarding everything you are afraid of losing.
You are standing before the Giver of Security. The future you fear is already in His hands. You are safe here.
The future you fear is in Allah's hands. You are safe here.
Verily, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest. - Surah Ar-Ra'd 13:28 — This salah is part of that remembrance.
Do not grive, indeed Allah is with us. - Surah At-Tawbah 9:40
Allah does not burden a soul more than it can bear. - Surah Al-Baqarah 2:286
So verily with hardship comes ease. Verily with hardship comes ease. - Surah Ash-Sharh 94:5-6
You've sometimes noticed anxiety about the future creeping into this Salah.
Worrying about what is coming has occasionally distracted you here.

llm_guidance.theme: Allah as the direct answer to fear of the unknown — He already holds what we are afraid of
llm_guidance.avoid: telling them anxiety is irrational, minimising their fears, generic reassurance
llm_guidance.tone: calming, direct, making Allah the shelter not just a concept

attributes.name: As-Samad
attributes.translation: The Eternal Refuge, The One to whom all turn in need

established.text: You are standing before Al-Qawiyy — the Strong. Your body is tired but you showed up. That is enough. He sees it.
You are standing before As-Samad, the One everyone and everything turns to in need. You turned to Him. That is the whole point.
You showed up tired. That effort is not lost on Allah.
You've noted tiredness during this Salah at times.
Tiredness has made this prayer feel heavy at times.

llm_guidance.theme: the act of showing up tired is itself an act of worship — Allah's strength carries what ours cannot
llm_guidance.avoid: pushing through, willpower framing, implying they should feel more energetic
llm_guidance.tone: affirming the effort, gentle, strength through surrender not exertion

attributes.name: Ar-Rahman
attributes.translation: The Entirely Merciful, The Most Compassionate

attributes.name: Al-Raheem
attributes.translation: The Most Merciful, The Especially Merciful

attributes.name: Al-Ghafur
attributes.translation: The Most Forgiving, The One whose forgiveness is unlimited, The One who forgives all sins

attributes.name: Al-Ghaffar
attributes.translation: The All Forgiving, The One who forgives often

established.text: You are standing before Ar-Rahman — the Entirely Merciful. Allah sees your struggle.
You are standing before Al-Raheem — the Especially Merciful, whose mercy is reserved for the believers. Your guilt brought you here. That is exactly where His mercy meets you.
You are standing before Al-Ghafur — the One whose forgiveness has no limit and no condition of worthiness. No regret is too heavy to bring here.
You are standing before Al-Ghaffar — the One who forgives again and again, without weariness. He does not tire of forgiving you. Do not tire of returning to him.
Allah says: 'I am just as My slave thinks I am... if he comes to Me walking, I go to him running.' - Sahih al-Bukhari 7405
'O My servants who have transgressed against themselves! Do not lose hope in the mercy of Allah, indeed Allah forgives all sins. He is indeed the All-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.'
Except those who repent, believe and do good deeds. Then for them Allah will replace their sins with good deeds. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful. - Surah Al-Furqan 25:70
Guilt of your past sins has occasionally distracted you in this Salah.
Your conscience of your past sins has sometimes made it difficult to focus in this Salah.

llm_guidance.theme: Allah's mercy and forgiveness are limitless and unconditional — guilt itself is a sign of faith, and this prayer is where your repentance starts
llm_guidance.avoid: minimising the weight of sin, false reassurance, shaming, implying the sin may be unforgivable
llm_guidance.tone: deeply merciful, welcoming, making the act of turning back to Allah feel like the most natural and expected response

attributes.name: Al-Haleem
attributes.translation: The Forbearing, The Patient, The Clement

attributes.name: As-Sabur
attributes.translation: The Patient, The One who does not hasten

established.text: You are standing before Al-Haleem — the Forbearing, the One who is never in a hurry. Slow down to meet Him.
You are standing before As-Sabur. He does not rush. This prayer does not need to be raced through — it needs to be given.
Allah is not in a hurry. Neither should you be.
The Prophet ﷺ said: "When you hear the iqamah, walk to the prayer with tranquility and dignity. Do not rush." (Bukhari 636)
You've sometimes felt rushed during this Salah.
The pace of your day has occasionally followed you into this prayer.

llm_guidance.theme: Allah's nature is unhurried — rushing is the opposite of the presence this moment calls for
llm_guidance.avoid: productivity framing, telling them to be more organised, stressing them further
llm_guidance.tone: slowing, permission-giving, making stillness feel like the right response

attributes.name: Al-Aleem
attributes.translation: The All-Knowing, aware of every thought

attributes.name: Al-Baseer
attributes.translation: The All-Seeing, The One who sees all things

established.text: You are standing before Al-Aleem — He who knows every secret and sees every turn of the heart. Even a wandering mind in front of Him is still in front of Him.
You are standing before Al-Baseer. He sees your effort to return your attention. Every return counts.
Every time you return your attention, it counts. Keep returning.
Your mind has sometimes wandered to random thoughts in this Salah.
Scattered thoughts have occasionally pulled you away here.

llm_guidance.theme: even a distracted mind that keeps returning is still in worship — Allah sees the effort not just the result
llm_guidance.avoid: shaming the mind for wandering, implying failure, perfectionism
llm_guidance.tone: forgiving, reframing distraction as an opportunity to return, normalising the struggle
